lead: A property access records the class the receiver was typed as, not the class that declared the property.
body: `nvs_types::expr::members::check_property_member` writes `ExprInfo::Property { class: qname }` from the receiver — right for `InstKind::FieldGet`, wrong for any per-property fact `nvs-ir` looks up by that label: an inherited `lateinit` read through a subclass answers `false` against the parent's own-only record and the guard is silently not emitted. Flatten such a table along the class graph where it is recorded; the failure is quiet, because a method that never touches `$this` runs fine on a null receiver.
